# M3-5: finbot calibrate

- Milestone: M3
- Branch / worktree: `t/M3-5`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M3-5`
- Depends on: M3-3 (M3-1a through M3-2 transitively)
- Touches (exclusive while running): calibrate/, cmd/ (new file `calibrate.go` plus subcommand dispatch)
- Plan refs: §3.3, R6, spikes/jev.md §Recommendation, BACKLOG "What the active plan means for M3"
- YNAB access: none (reads the local mirror)
- Deploy: no (smoke: none; ships in M3-17)

## Goal
`finbot calibrate` measures precision and coverage for the rules + Jev stack on labelled history and writes a versioned
`calibrate/calibration.json` holding τ. There is no old→new mapping (Brendan, 2026-11-08).

## Where the labelled data comes from
`store.LabeledHistory` over the active plan plus every plan with `has_discretionary` true in `plan_scan`. A label counts for its exact
active-plan category name. A label with no matching category (`in_active_list=false`) stays in the set as a **hard negative**: if the
stack would auto-apply it, that's a false positive. Not hard negatives, and left out entirely by passing the policy's set-aside names as `excludedNames`: Ready to
Assign, Credit Card Payments, internal categories and set-asides. A historical `Christmas` label has no fair verdict: §3.2 says that spending is now `Discretionary`, so predicting that isn't wrong.

## Scope
- Apply the runtime guardrails and rules first. τ is fitted only on what reaches the model, and rule precision is reported separately.
- No leakage: payee history and rules for a transaction use only labels dated before it. Calibrate and the runtime share the same code path.
- Split by time: oldest 70% tunes, newest 30% holds out. τ is the smallest value on a 0.50-0.99 grid whose tuning-set Wilson 95% lower bound
  on precision is ≥ 0.85.
- `auto_eligible` is true only if the tuning set has at least 200 model-band rows and the holdout's point precision is ≥ 0.85.
- Also report the top-3 hit rate, per-source row counts, the hard-negative count and how many were auto-applied at τ, and per-category precision.
- Output JSON: model, policy_hash, candidates_hash, τ, precision, coverage, n, auto_eligible, created_at. Names and aggregates only: no ids, payees or
  memos. Embed it and expose `calibrate.Current()`, with a checked-in placeholder at `auto_eligible=false`.
- Jev is reached through `classify.Model`, batched, with a `--limit` flag.

## Out of scope
- Running on real data (M3-6). Calibrating the claude second opinion (Plan question 1).

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Fixture test with a fake Model: known probabilities yield the expected τ, precision and coverage.
- [ ] Test: a hard negative above τ lowers precision; a set-aside or Ready to Assign label never enters the set.
- [ ] Test: a transaction never sees history dated on or after itself.
- [ ] Tests: fewer than 200 rows, or a holdout under 0.85, gives `auto_eligible=false`.
- [ ] Test: the output JSON contains no id, payee or memo from the fixture.
- [ ] go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... green

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - New `calibrate/` (`calibrate.go`): `Run` routes labelled history oldest-first through `classify.Guard`, then
    `classify.Rules.Decide`, then `classify.Model` (batched, `Batch` per call) using `Rules.NewTxn` (the runtime's code
    path). Rules and payee history for a row are built only from labels dated strictly before it (same-day siblings
    excluded). Policy set-aside labels (e.g. historical `Christmas`) are dropped; labels not among the candidates are hard
    negatives. Oldest 70% tunes (cut moved forward so no date straddles it), newest 30% holds out; τ = smallest grid value
    0.50–0.99 with tuning Wilson-95 lower bound ≥ 0.85; `auto_eligible` = τ found ∧ ≥ 200 tuning model-band rows ∧ holdout
    point precision ≥ 0.85.
  - Output `Calibration` (version, model, policy_hash, candidates_hash, tau (null if none), precision, coverage, n,
    auto_eligible, created_at) plus a `report`: tune/holdout sizes, per-source counts, guard skips, rule precision,
    top-3 hit rate, hard negatives and how many were auto-applied, per-category precision (predicted names only).
    `precision`/`coverage` are the holdout model band at τ; `n` is rows evaluated.
  - `calibrate/current.go`: embedded `calibration.json` (checked-in placeholder, `auto_eligible=false`, `tau=null`),
    `Current()`, `Parse`, `Calibration.Applies(model, policyHash, candidatesHash, pTop)` (all must match), atomic `WriteFile`.
  - `calibrate/load.go`: `Inputs` = candidates of the active plan + `LabeledHistory` over the active plan then each
    `has_discretionary` plan, deduped (supervisor note), candidate names as active names, set-asides as excluded.
  - `cmd/calibrate.go`: `finbot calibrate [--limit N] [--batch N] [--out calibrate/calibration.json]`; needs
    `FINBOT_DB_PATH`, `YNAB_BUDGET_ID`, `JEV_API_KEY`; prints names/aggregates only, scrubs plan id and key. Usage text updated.
- Acceptance:
  - Fake-model fixture → τ 0.71, precision 0.9, coverage 0.5556: pass (`go test ./calibrate -run TestRunFitsTauPrecisionCoverage`)
  - Hard negative above τ lowers precision (1 → 0.8889): pass (`-run TestRunHardNegativeAboveTauLowersPrecision`);
    set-aside/RTA/CC never enter the set: pass (`-run 'TestRunDropsSetAsideLabels|TestInputsLabelSet'`)
  - No history on/after the row's date: pass (`-run 'TestRunNoLeakage|TestRunRulesSeeOnlyEarlierLabels'`)
  - < 200 tuning rows / holdout 0.8 → `auto_eligible=false`: pass (`-run 'TestRunNotEligible'`)
  - Output JSON has no id, payee, memo, account or hard-negative name: pass (`-run TestOutputHasNoIdsPayeesOrMemos`,
    `go test ./cmd -run TestCalibrateCmd`)
  - `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...`: pass
- Deviations from brief:
  - Guardrails run on a `TransactionDetail` rebuilt from `LabeledRow`, so: no account type (debt-account payment
    heuristics can't fire; CC-group and transfer rows are already excluded by `LabeledHistory`), no locks (every
    labelled row carries a human lock by definition), and `LabeledRow.Payee` is already normalized (lower case), so the
    P2P person-name check (`personShaped`) never fires on history; descriptor P2P (venmo, zelle…) does.
  - "In active list" means "is a classifier candidate": a label in a hidden active category counts as a hard negative,
    since the runtime can't choose it.
  - `cmd/app_test.go`: `TestMain_UsageExits2` used `calibrate` as its unknown-command example; changed to `bogus`.
- Follow-ups for backlog:
  - `store.LabeledRow` could carry the raw payee and account type so calibration guardrails match runtime exactly (P2P names).
  - Runtime (M3 categorize wiring) should gate with `calibrate.Current().Applies(...)`.
  - Wire `JEV_API_KEY` into config/deploy (already M3-17).
